\label{lemma-flat-at-point}
The property of morphisms of germs
$$
\mathcal{P}((X, x) \to (S, s)) =
\mathcal{O}_{S, s} \to \mathcal{O}_{X, x}\text{ is flat}
$$
is \'etale local on the source-and-target.

final_content.statement: A morphism of germs $(X,x)\to(S,s)$ is represented by a scheme map $U\to S$ on a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$, modulo agreement after shrinking $U$. A property $\mathcal Q$ of germ morphisms is *étale-local on source-and-target* if it is invariant under every commutative square of germ morphisms with both vertical arrows étale. The property that the induced local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat is étale-local on source-and-target for morphisms of germs, i.e. invariant under commutative squares of germs with étale vertical maps.
hypotheses: Commutative diagram of germ maps with étale vertical arrows.
conclusions: Flatness of the local homomorphism is equivalent across the square.

The induced fibre morphism $U'_{v'}\to U_v$ is étale.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-dimension-at-point}
Let $d \in \{0, 1, 2, \ldots, \infty\}$.
The property of morphisms of germs
$$
\mathcal{P}_d((X, x) \to (S, s))
\Leftrightarrow
\dim_x (X_s) = d
$$
is \'etale local on the source-and-target.

final_content.statement: A morphism of germs $(X,x)\to(S,s)$ is represented by a scheme map $U\to S$ on a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$, modulo agreement after shrinking $U$. A property $\mathcal Q$ of germ morphisms is *étale-local on source-and-target* if it is invariant under every commutative square of germ morphisms with both vertical arrows étale. Let $d\in\{0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$. For a germ $(X,x)\to(S,s)$, let $\dim_x(X_s)$ denote the minimum Krull dimension among open neighbourhoods of $x$ in the fibre $X_s$ (the dimension of the fibre germ at $x$), not the dimension of its local ring. The property $\dim_x(X_s)=d$ is étale-local on source-and-target for germs.
hypotheses: d is nonnegative or infinity, with étale vertical germ morphisms.
conclusions: The dimension of the fibre germ is preserved.

semantic_review_note: The pinned descent.tex L8062, by contrast to the local-ring-dimension lemma, asserts that the dimension dim_x(X_s) of the FIBRE GERM at x is invariant under étale changes of source and target. The proposed definition as the minimum dimensions of open neighbourhoods, d∈{0,1,...,∞}, and bidirectional locality accurately preserve that distinction.
